title: Synthesis and Characterization of mRNA-Loaded Poly(Beta Aminoesters) Nanoparticles for Vaccination Purposes
protocol: Add 5-amino-1-pentanol and 1-hexylamine into a round-bottom glass flask (100 mL).
Add 1,4-butanediol diacrylate to the mixture in the flask.
Pre-heat silicone oil bath at 90 °C.
Place the round-bottom flask into the pre-heated oil bath.
Stir the mixture overnight with a magnetic stir bar.
Take the product from the round-bottom flask and place it in the freezer at -20 °C.
Add 25 mL of 0.1 M HCl to selected peptides, e.g., peptide Cys-His-His-His with Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), into a previously weighed 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Manually stir the mixture overnight to obtain a clear solution.
Freeze the solution at -80 °C for 1 h.
Freeze-dry the resulting peptide hydrochloride.
Make a solution of C6-pBAE (0.031 mmol) in dimethyl sulfoxide.
Make a solution of the peptide hydrochloride (0.078 mmol) in dimethyl sulfoxide.
Mix the two solutions in a screw cap tube and screw on the cap.
Stir the mixture solution in a water bath at 25 °C for 20 h with a magnetic stir bar.
Add the mixture to a 7:3 (v/v) diethyl ether/acetone solution.
Centrifuge the resulting suspension at 25,000 x g at 4 °C to remove the solvent.
Wash the solid with 7:3 (v/v) diethyl ether/acetone twice.
Dry the product under a vacuum (<0.2 atm).
Make a solution of 100 mg/mL of the product in dimethyl sulfoxide.
Name the resulting product as C6-peptide-pBAE.
Validate the structure of the obtained polymer through 1H-NMR to confirm the disappearance of the olefin signals associated with terminal acrylates.
If not used, freeze the polymer at -20 °C.
Thaw the polymers C6-peptide-pBAE and vortex the solution.
Pipette the polymer mix up and down to prepare a 12.5 mM (V1) solution in sodium acetate (NaAc).
Vortex the mixture and wait for 10 min.
Prepare the mRNA at 0.5 mg/mL and mix by pipetting (V2).
Mix the genetic material solution and C6-peptide-pBAE solution in a ratio of 1:1 (Vi = V1 + V2).
Load the C6-peptide-pBAE into a microcentrifuge tube where the mRNA is added by pipetting up and down for mixing.
Incubate at 25 °C for 30 min in a thermoblock.
Precipitate with RNase-free water by adding an equal volume as the mixture of mRNA and pBAE (Vi).
Add the same volume as the mixture of mRNA and pBAE (Vi) in HEPES 20 mM and sucrose 4% by pipetting up and down for mixing.
Freeze at -80 °C freezer of the previous polyplex solution for 1 h.
Perform primary drying:
- Incubate for 1 h at -60 °C and 0.001 hPa.
- Incubate for 1 h at -40 °C and 0.0001 hPa.
- Incubate for 4 h at -20 °C and 0.0001 hPa.
- Incubate for 12 h at 5 °C and 0.0001 hPa.
Store the polyplexes at -20 °C immediately to avoid rehydration until use.
Reconstitute lyophilized C6-peptide-pBAE nanoparticles with DEPC water at the moment of use.
Pipette gently until total resuspension, ensuring no material remains on the vial wall.
Mix vigorously up and down to avoid bubbles.
Ensure the sample has a transparent to translucent appearance.
Store the samples on ice or at 4°C for a maximum period of 24 hours once reconstituted.
Mix mRNA and pBAE thoroughly by pipetting to a final concentration of 0.25 mg/mL.
Pre-rinse a microcuvette with filtered dilution media.
Fill the cuvette with at least 50 µL of the sample solution and cap it.
Introduce the sample inside the DLS instrument, ensuring the cell is correctly inserted.
Open the Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) file and introduce the desired Sample Name.
Select Size Measurement.
Run the particle size measurement using DLS by clicking on Play.
After the triple beep sounds, select the results corresponding to the sample.
Obtain the average particle size, average PDI, standard deviation, and graphics from the selected results.
Remove the cell from DLS equipment.
Remove the sample for zeta-potential analysis.
Clean and rinse the cell with deionized water.
Dry the cleaned cuvette under a compressed air gas stream.
Mix mRNA and pBAE thoroughly to prepare nanoparticles with a final concentration of mRNA at 0.25 mg/mL.
Freeze and dry the nanoparticle solution.
Resuspend the lyophilized nanoparticle sample using water.
Dilute the resuspended sample by mixing it with water in a ratio of 1:10 (final concentration 0.025 mg/mL).
Pre-rinse a disposable folded capillary cell with filtered dilution media to clean it from impurities.
Fill the cuvette with diluted nanoparticles using a 1 mL syringe, ensuring there are no bubbles.
Insert the filled cuvette into the DLS instrument.
Open the SOP file for zeta potential analysis and enter the desired Sample Name.
Select Zeta-Potential Measurement in the SOP file.
Run the zeta-potential measurement by clicking Play.
Select the results corresponding to the sample on the measurement sheet.
Obtain the average zeta-potential, standard deviation, and graphics.
Remove the cell from the DLS equipment.
Clean and rinse the cuvette cell with deionized water.
Rinse the cuvette cell with ethanol.
Clean and rinse the cuvette cell again with deionized water.
Dry the cleaned cuvette under a compressed air gas stream.
Switch on the computer and the equipment.
Check whether all components are plugged in correctly.
Open the recommended software.
Connect the Top plate, here the O-ring cell, into the laser module.
Avoid overscrewing this part.
Load the chamber with buffer and/or deionized water using a 1 mL syringe.
Repeat the loading procedure at least two times.
Prepare the sample by diluting it 1/1000 in deionized water from the concentration used in DLS size measurement.
Prepare at least 1 mL of the diluted sample.
Load the diluted sample into a 1 mL syringe, avoiding introducing bubbles.
Load the samples into the chamber using a syringe.
Plug the laser module into the NTA big chamber.
In the Hardware settings, check that the Camera and Blue Laser 488 nm are selected.
Start with the camera level at 0 and press Start Camera on the Capture window.
Adjust the beam position to move up and down on the screen as needed.
Avoid oversaturated pixels by adjusting the Camera Level.
Focus using the lateral wheel for better particle visualization, aiming for particles with a halo.
Adjust the concentration to have between 10 to 100 particles per field.
Go to the Measurement Selection-SOP window in the software and select Standard Measurement.
Provide a name and folder path (on Base filename) to save the records of the sample.
Press Create and Run Script once the SOP parameters are correctly set up.
Add another fraction of the sample by pushing the syringe's plunger after the first replicate is measured.
Repeat the process for a third time to analyze the third replicate.
Readjust the Screen Gain and Detection Threshold after completing the three measures.
Export the results in a pdf file once the analysis is completed.
Clean the NTA chamber by repeatedly flushing with water until no particles are observed.
Flush the buffer used (PBS) to prepare for subsequent measurements.
Flush air inside the chamber and dry it with microscopic grade paper at the end of the day.
Drop 10 µL of sample on a carbon-coated copper grid.
Let the droplet dry for 10 min.
Remove excess liquid by softly tapping on filter paper if necessary.
Drop 10 μL of uranyl acetate (2% w/v) solution for negative staining.
Let it dry for 1 minute.
Remove the liquid excess by softly tapping on filter paper if necessary.
Introduce the sample into the microscope and scan at a voltage operation of 80 kV.
Prepare nanoparticles at the desired concentration, freeze and dry them, then resuspend and dilute to a final concentration of 6 µg/mL.
Dilute TE buffer from the 20x stock solution according to the formula Vt = (number of samples x 100 μL x 4) / ((number of samples x 290 μL) + 2 mL).
Prepare TE buffer with 3 µg/µL of heparin from a stock of 100 µg/μL according to the formula Vt = Number of samples x 50 μL x 2.
Prepare an RNA standard ranging from 0.2 µg/mL to 0.025 µg/mL in 1x Tris-EDTA (TE) buffer.
Prepare RNA:pBAE standard with heparin as specified in Table S1B.
Prepare Heparin standard as detailed in Table S1C.
Load 295 μL of TE buffer into the first lane of a 96-well plate for each sample to be analyzed.
Load 50 μL of 1x TE buffer into lanes B and C (duplicates for each sample).
Load 50 µL of 1x TBE buffer with 3 µg/µL of Heparin into lanes D and E.
Load 100 µL of each standard in lanes F, G, and H.
Load 5 µL of each sample in lane A at a concentration of 0.1 µg/mL.
Mix properly by pipetting.
Load 50 µL of each sample on the four wells below, with two containing 50 µL of buffer 1x TE and two more containing 1x TE buffer with 3 µg/µL of Heparin.
Incubate the sample for 30 min at 37 °C.
Prepare RiboGreen reagent as per the manufacturer's protocol in 1x TE buffer.
Dilute the RiboGreen reagent 1:200 and vortex.
Protect the RiboGreen reagent from light.
Load 100 µL of RiboGreen solution into each well.
Detect fluorescence using the microplate reader with an excitation wavelength of 500 nm and an emission wavelength of 525 nm.
Place the 96-well plate onto the microscope after 24 h of transfection.
Visualize cells with the 10x objective using transmission mode (bright field).
Adjust the focus on the cells.
Apply a white balance to reference the software about the background of the samples.
Acquire an image for overlay during analysis.
Change the microscope mode to reflection mode (fluorescence).
Move the filter wheel to the blue laser (488 nm) to visualize eGFP.
Adjust Gain between 3 and 5 to avoid artifacts and excess on background signal.
Adjust Exposure time based on transfection efficiency (from ms to 1 s).
Acquire images for all conditions or wells using the same exposure time.
Use a multichannel pipette to prepare the 96-well plate for the flow cytometry experiment.
Recover all media volume if working with semi-adherent cells and store it in another 96-well plate.
Clean HeLa cells with 100 µL/well of 1x PBS.
Aspire the cleaned solution from the wells.
Add 25 µL/well of trypsin.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.
Add previously recovered media to stop trypsin action and fix the cells.
Add 31.25 µL/well of formalin 10% for 20 min (final concentration 2.5%).
Visualize the state of the cells by microscopy.
Pipette up and down several times to ensure cell detachment and avoid agglomeration.
Turn on the flow cytometer and the software.
Set up proper conditions in the software for the experiment.
Mix one cycle every 1 min during analysis.
Rinse one cycle every well between samples.
Check if there are enough buffers available.
Ensure all components of the cytometer are correctly connected.
View the flow data on FSC versus SCC scatter plot to distinguish cells from debris.
Plot another scatter plot comparing amplitude (FSC-A) versus height (FSC-H) to gate and discriminate individual cells.
Plate 10,000 cells/well in a 96-well plate the day before transfection.
Let the cells attach to the plate for at least 12 hours.
Prepare pBAEs NPs as described to transfect 0.6 μg mRNA per well.
Transfect cells using a transfection reagent with 0.1 μg mRNA and 0.25 μL of the transfection reagent per well.
Incubate the 96-well plate for 24 hours in a dry air incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Recover the cells after 24-hour incubation and save them in another well or plate.
Wash the cells remaining on the well with 25 µL of 1x PBS.
Aspire the PBS and add 25 µL of trypsin.
Incubate the plate for 5 min at 37 °C.
Stop the trypsin reaction by adding the previously recovered media onto the correspondent well.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspire the media.
Add 50 µL/well of a 1x PBS and 2.5% formalin.
Incubate it at 4 °C for 20 min to fix cells.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 x g for 5 min.
Aspire the media.
Add 50 µL/well of 1x PBS and 3% BSA (Blocking buffer).
Incubate for 30 min at 4 °C.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 x g for 5 min.
Aspire the media.
Add 50 µL/well of the primary antibody (mouse α-OVA) in 1x PBS and 3% BSA.
Incubate for 30 min at 4 °C.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 x g for 5 min.
Aspire the media.
Add secondary antibodies solution (α-mouse-AlexaFluor488/PerCP and Cy5.5-CD11b/APC-CD86) in 1x PBS and 3% BSA.
Incubate it for 1 h at 4 °C.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 x g for 5 min.
Wash the cells with 50 µL/well of 1x PBS.
Centrifuge (400 x g for 5 min).
Aspire and then resuspend the cells in 100 µL/well of 1x PBS and 2.5% Formalin.
Analyze it by flow cytometry, as described above.
